clue.text: Reward for valour secured by a round or rounds?

indicators.note: a thing secured by others is held between them, so the medal sits inside the other letters

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O
MM is the Military Medal, a British award for bravery

explanation.surface: A soldier's medal for bravery is earned in one round of fire, or several.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'rounds' here means bullets, not stages of a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammunition is counted in rounds, and the slang short form covers bullets and shells generally.

clue.text: Maritime plant to spoil area of little water around mouth of Mersey

parts.note: to mar something is to spoil it

indicators.note: around says the shallow wraps about the letter from the river

parts.note: a shallow is a stretch where the water is not deep

indicators.note: the mouth of a river is where it begins its meeting with the sea, here the first letter of the name

explanation.surface: Someone frets that a coastal plant might ruin the shallows at the Mersey estuary.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mersey is the river that runs out to sea at Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: This mallow species grows in salt marshes near coasts, hence a seaside plant.

clue.text: Admit cry of distress on picking up wordplay

parts.note: ow is what someone cries when hurt

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking up lifts the word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a pun is a piece of play on words

explanation.surface: A solver confesses to groaning upon spotting a pun in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To confess something is to come clean about it, the phrasal verb used here.

clue.text: Biscuit small animals store for winter, perhaps

parts.note: shrews are tiny insect-eating mammals
to bury food is one way of storing it for winter, as squirrels do; perhaps marks the example

explanation.surface: Little creatures hoard a biscuit away for the cold months.
explanation.walkthrough: A Shrewsbury biscuit is a crisp, lemony British shortbread-style biscuit named after the Shropshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a named variety of sweet baked biscuit, so the type is given by its category.

clue.text: Alarm about soldiers is evident in club for American women

indicators.note: about means going round, so the distress call surrounds the soldiers

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal
OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Soldiers sound an alarm inside a women's club in America.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorosis is a US women's society or club, named after the first such organisation.

clue.text: Some avoid arguments raised in broadcast

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised turns the run so it reads upwards
some of the letters of the phrase supply the answer, a run inside avoid arguments

explanation.surface: Some people shun arguments that come up on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio is a broadcast medium, and as a verb it means to transmit a message.

clue.text: Scottish churchman to go about covered in iron

parts.note: to go is a coy phrase for urinating, which is to wee

indicators.note: covered in says the word for about is wrapped by the chemical symbol

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A Scottish minister has to relieve himself while clad in iron.
explanation.walkthrough: A Wee Free is a member of the Free Church of Scotland, a strict Presbyterian body.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname refers to members of a minority Scottish Presbyterian denomination, so a churchman qualifies.

clue.text: Instrument playing after prohibition ended

indicators.note: after places the word for playing behind the other two

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition
done means finished or ended
on means playing, as a show is on

explanation.surface: An instrument struck up again once a ban was lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: The bandoneon is a squeeze-box of the concertina family, central to tango music.

clue.text: Long-term prisoner picked up litre for a further drink

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up lifts the word so it reads upwards

parts.note: a lifer is someone serving a life sentence

explanation.surface: A lifer was hoisted up after downing a litre, ready for another round.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-up of a glass is another serving of drink, the noun sense used here.

clue.text: Place to visit museums, even before the game

indicators.note: before puts the word for even ahead of the game

parts.note: to iron is to even out or smooth
bridge is the card game

explanation.surface: Visit the museums, even though it means getting there before the match.
explanation.walkthrough: Ironbridge in Shropshire has a cluster of museums of the Industrial Revolution by its famous iron bridge over the Severn.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ironbridge Gorge is a World Heritage site with ten museums, so a museum destination.

clue.text: Dreadful Northern fellows surrounding one

parts.note: a means one
F is fellow, doubled as FF for the plural

explanation.surface: Some awful northern blokes are crowding round someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Naff is British slang for tacky or rubbish, hence awful.

clue.text: Nick's time at work involving work on line

indicators.note: involving means containing, so the work period holds the other letters

parts.note: a shift is a spell of working time
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: Nick's work shift includes a stint on the production line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a man's name with a possessive; it is the verb meaning steal.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is British slang for to steal, and this verb means stealing from a store.

clue.text: Town recreation includes series of matches

indicators.note: includes says the word for recreation contains the series

parts.note: sport is recreation or games
a tour is a series of matches played abroad by a touring team

explanation.surface: A town's leisure offering takes in a run of fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: Stourport-on-Severn is a Worcestershire canal town.
explanation.definitionFit: Stourport is an English market town in Worcestershire, on the River Severn.

clue.text: Score, getting runs in hand — a cause for celebration?

parts.note: a score is twenty

indicators.note: in places the runs inside the hand

parts.note: a fist is a clenched hand
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A batter scoring with runs in hand has reason to celebrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A twenty-first birthday is a traditional coming-of-age party, so a reason for festivities.

clue.text: Nothing found in location of a dip or severe descent

indicators.note: found in says the zero lies inside the bathing place

parts.note: baths are a public swimming pool, where one takes a dip
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing is found at a bathing spot or a steep slope downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathos is a ludicrous drop from the lofty to the trivial in style, an anticlimax.

clue.text: Greeting love with weary shuffling in time that appears endless

indicators.note: in places the love and rearranged letters inside the time word
endless means the last letter of the time word is dropped

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: shuffling means the letters of weary are rearranged

explanation.surface: A weary lover shuffles through an apparently endless hour of greetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love' is tennis zero; 'that appears endless' drops the last letter of the time word, and 'in' sets the shuffled weary, led by love, inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: The question is a standard salutation on meeting someone, a conventional hello.

clue.text: Woman joining her forerunner in Western Region at any time

indicators.note: in places the two women inside the region

parts.note: WR stands for Western Region, a former British Railways region
hen is a slang word for a woman
Eve, the first woman, is the forerunner of all women

explanation.surface: A woman teams up with her predecessor on the Western Region railway, whenever.
explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction means no matter when, on every occasion that something happens.

clue.text: Query dairy product English exported

indicators.note: exported means sent out, so the English letter leaves

parts.note: whey is the liquid left after cheesemaking

explanation.surface: Someone asks about an English dairy product being sold abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the standard interrogative asking for a reason, so a question.

clue.text: Means to follow calamity with a surprise

indicators.note: to follow puts the word for means after the other pieces

parts.note: a blow is a setback or calamity
a way is a means of doing something

explanation.surface: Someone plans to follow a disaster with a twist.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish or amaze someone is the informal phrasal verb's sense here.

clue.text: Struggle with tossing, abandoning ship

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving, so the ship letters are taken out

parts.note: tossing and turning in bed is being restless
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: Sailors grapple with rolling seas as they abandon ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple or fight hard, physically or mentally, is to struggle.

clue.text: I note returns in tax year implying self-satisfaction

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the tax and year

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the pair reads backwards

explanation.surface: Filing tax returns for the year shows a smug self-regard.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanity is excessive pride in oneself, conceit or complacency.

clue.text: Minister upset as Queen is seen with the writer and painter

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the title upside down

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a minister
the writer refers to the setter, me
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A clergyman is distressed to see the Queen with the writer and an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Johannes Vermeer was the Dutch Golden Age master of Girl with a Pearl Earring.

clue.text: City in cowboy film cut down after invasion by monstrous creature

indicators.note: after invasion by means the creature has got inside the shortened film
cut down means shortened, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a western is a cowboy film
an orc is a monster of fantasy fiction

explanation.surface: A city appears in a cut cowboy film after a monster attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Worcester is a cathedral city in the English West Midlands on the River Severn.

clue.text: Namely, an instruction for dealing with breakdown?

definitions.meaning: namely means that is to say, introducing a specification

definitions.text: an instruction for dealing with breakdown?
definitions.meaning: read as two words, an order to tow a broken-down vehicle

explanation.definitionFit: The formal phrase means that is to say; split, it tells a recovery driver to haul the car.

clue.text: See 11
Identify murder victim found beneath lake

indicators.note: in a down clue, found beneath puts the victim under the lake letter

parts.note: Abel was killed by his brother Cain in Genesis

explanation.surface: Police identify a murder victim discovered under a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: To tag or name something is to identify it, the verb sense.

clue.text: Small Greek character dodging rebellion

indicators.note: dodging means avoiding, so the Greek letter is left out

parts.note: a mutiny is a rebellion
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A small Greek man avoids taking part in an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiny is very little, minute or small.

clue.text: See 8
Abbey rejected feeble busker, sadly, before end of day

indicators.note: before puts the busker letters ahead of the day's last letter
rejected means turned back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: wet is British slang for feeble or weedy

indicators.note: sadly signals the letters of busker go wrong and are rearranged
end of picks the final letter of day

explanation.surface: An abbey turns away a pathetic busker, sadly, at dusk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns WET into TEW; 'sadly' makes KESBUR from BUSKER.
explanation.definitionFit: Tewkesbury Abbey is a great Norman church in Gloucestershire, often called by the town name alone.

clue.text: German left to rescue unhappily blinded nobleman

indicators.note: unhappily signals the letters of to rescue are rearranged

explanation.surface: A German left to rescue a blinded nobleman, but it went badly.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's King Lear the Earl of Gloucester has his eyes put out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl in King Lear is the lord whose eyes are gouged out, a noble title.

clue.text: Item 8 at auction — not inclined?

parts.note: a lot is an item put up for sale at auction
H is the eighth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Bidders seem reluctant to go for item eight at an auction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Item 8 at auction' reads as Lot H, lots being labelled in order, H being the eighth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Loth is a variant spelling meaning reluctant or unwilling.
